solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tricky problem from head of Stradivarius fiddle

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of Stradivarius is used

parts.note: to fiddle with something is to tinker with it

explanation.surface: A tough puzzle is posed by the top of a precious Stradivarius violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinker is informal for something very difficult, such as a nasty exam question.

clue.text: Suffered pain in the neck

definitions.meaning: past tense of bear: endured, put up with
a tedious, tiresome person or thing

explanation.surface: Someone endured an aching neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore is the past tense of bear, meaning endured; a bore is also a tiresome nuisance.

clue.text: Virgin's pursued, reportedly

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like the clue's synonym

parts.note: pursued means chased

explanation.surface: A tabloid line claiming a virgin was being chased.
explanation.definitionFit: A virgin is sexually pure, which is the adjective's core sense of abstaining from sex.

clue.text: Mystery of hound with no end, strangely

indicators.note: letters arranged strangely are placed in an unexpected new order
with no end means the last letter of the word with is dropped

explanation.surface: A puzzling tale about a dog that lacks a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end' gives WIT; 'strangely' rearranges HOUND plus WIT; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective story built around who committed the crime is a classic mystery genre.

clue.text: Great unrest with demo out of control

indicators.note: letters out of control are in disorder, so these words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Serious civil unrest as a demonstration gets out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous is a synonym for great in the sense of huge or excellent.

clue.text: Lower level in Scottish river

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, so the level word sits within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Aberdeenshire, Scotland
level means flat

explanation.surface: The water level drops in a river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflate something is to let air out, bringing it down; lower here is a verb.

clue.text: Decline Academy's opening award

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Academy is used

parts.note: a trophy is an award such as a cup

explanation.surface: Someone turns down the prize that launches an Academy season.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is wasting away or deterioration, a gradual decline in strength or size.

clue.text: Spun news for the audience

indicators.note: what is meant for an audience is heard, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: word can mean news, as in 'any word from home?'

explanation.surface: A PR team puts a spin on announcements made to the listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that whirred turned rapidly with a buzzing noise, as a spinning wheel does.

clue.text: Line up vessels for giving praise

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned around

parts.note: a row is a line
shipping is a collective word for ships

explanation.surface: Boats are arranged in a row as part of a religious ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipping means venerating or adoring, offering devotion and praise to a deity.

clue.text: Concluded being taken in by bounder's too demeaning

indicators.note: the answer is taken in, or held, by the run of letters in these clue words

explanation.surface: Someone decided they were being duped by a cad's too-belittling manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To have understood something can mean to have inferred or gathered it, i.e. reached a conclusion.

clue.text: Country's military acted largely independently initially

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the words that come before it

explanation.surface: A nation's army has taken matters into its own hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a West African nation, whose army has indeed seized power in coups.

clue.text: Judge again almost remains putting innocent fools inside

indicators.note: putting one piece inside means it is placed within the trimmed remains word
almost means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: rest means remains or remainder
asses are silly, naive people

explanation.surface: A judge, nearly finished, is reconsidering by bringing in some simpletons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a court official, but here it is a verb; 'putting' is only a link before 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate or appraise once more.

clue.text: Girlfriend, the woman welcoming little time on technique

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: she is a pronoun for a woman
wee is Scottish for little
art can mean technique or skill

explanation.surface: A woman greets her girlfriend briefly before discussing method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets ART after the rest, as in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a beloved partner, used often of a boyfriend or girlfriend.

clue.text: Two characters or six from Latin in etymology

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the stretch of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: A note on word origins: two letters or six come from Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: As a Roman numeral the number is XC, two characters; spelt out it has six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The number is written XC in Roman numerals, two symbols, or as a six-letter word.

clue.text: Do nice strip perhaps showing outline

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be put another way, rearranged

explanation.surface: A strip cartoon that looks nice, as a sketch outlined.
explanation.definitionFit: A description is an account or outline of what something is like.

clue.text: Skill seen in Crown Derby for example

parts.note: a crown is a cap, as on a tooth
Derby is an English city, so it is an example of a city

explanation.surface: Craftsmanship shown in Royal Crown Derby porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Crown Derby is a famous English porcelain maker; here Crown and Derby are split up.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity can mean ability or competence, the power to do something well.

clue.text: Ankara chiefly includes former capital city

indicators.note: the words Ankara chiefly include, or contain, the run of letters needed

explanation.surface: Ankara mostly contains a capital that once was.
explanation.definitionFit: Karachi was Pakistan's first capital until Rawalpindi and then Islamabad replaced it.

clue.text: Out of control in craft at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Panic aboard a boat on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means wild with fear or worry, behaving in a frenzied, uncontrolled way.

clue.text: Drink with container overturned. Apple perhaps?

parts.note: to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does

indicators.note: something overturned is upended, so the container word is read backwards

parts.note: a pot is a container

explanation.surface: Spilling a drink by knocking over its pot onto a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple makes the MacBook, a portable computer, so the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Prayer certain to produce happiness

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request or prayer
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A prayer guaranteed to bring joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is a feeling of enjoyment or contentment, close to happiness.

clue.text: Queen, group falling from grace

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth
a ring is a group, especially of conspirators

explanation.surface: A monarch's circle is tainted by scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring means sinning or doing wrong, i.e. lapsing from a state of virtue.

clue.text: Secretary, say, returning call

parts.note: PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the abbreviation is turned around

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: An assistant ringing someone back.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to summon them, by loudspeaker or pager.

clue.text: Illegal traffic of criminal gang pinching paintings back

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing in, so the reversed art is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a band is a gang

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: art means paintings collectively

explanation.surface: A crime gang steals artworks and smuggles them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband means smuggled goods or illicit trading, the traffic of banned items.

clue.text: 'Inter' football team?

definitions.meaning: to inter is to put in the grave
... FC is a football club from ..., a town in Greater Manchester

explanation.surface: Is Inter Milan the football team in question?
explanation.walkthrough: Inter Milan is an Italian football club, which makes 'Inter' look like a team; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury is to inter a body; Bury is also an English football club in Lancashire.

clue.text: A number eating seconds dehydrated

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the seconds letter goes into the number

parts.note: thirty is a number

explanation.surface: A crowd wolfing down second helpings and craving a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dehydrated means short of water, which brings on the craving to drink.

clue.text: Ran odd broadcast about 'I, Robot'

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the single letter
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A station aired a strange programme about the Asimov book I, Robot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns RANODD into ANDROD, and 'about' puts it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a humanlike robot, a staple of science fiction.
